summary: A local news roundup of ten green public transportation initiatives planned for the area, spanning electric and hydrogen buses, solar transit stations, e-bikes, contactless payments, autonomous shuttles, high-speed rail, green corridors, cable cars and electric water transport. Each project is tied to a named leader and a timeline running from late 2023 to 2026. The article stresses lower emissions and accessibility for all riders.
one_line: Overview of ten upcoming local green transit projects, from electric buses and hydrogen fuel cell buses to cable cars and water taxis, timed 2023-2026.
key_facts: Since September 2023 the local transit authority has expanded its electric bus fleet under the Green Wheels Initiative, championed by Transit Director Sandra Klimt, aiming to replace half of the gas-powered buses by 2025.
The new electric buses have low-entry floors and improved wheelchair securing systems.

Designer and civic planner Jacob Moreno proposed solar-powered transit stations, with construction set to begin in early 2024, powering lighting, ticket kiosks and real-time information screens while providing shade.
The local bike-share program, first introduced in 2022, will add 500 e-bikes in spring 2024, as announced by city council member Aisha Nguyen.
The Smart Transit Access Program, led by tech entrepreneur Mark Gillespie, is slated to launch a contactless multi-modal payment system in late 2023 covering buses, trains and shared scooters.
An autonomous electric shuttle pilot program launches in spring 2024, with AI-directed routing; mobility expert Dr. Linda Cho says it will reduce travel time and congestion.
The high-speed rail network, championed by Governor Mark Henderson, is set to become operational by 2026 with electric propulsion and aims to cut intercity travel time by half.

City planner Roger Stevens and the local transportation department are developing downtown "Green Corridors" expected to open by mid-2024, reserved for nonmotorized transport and electric public vehicles.
Hydrogen fuel cell buses, which emit only water vapor, will hit the streets in summer 2024; transit official Gary Yung says they can significantly reduce reliance on fossil fuels.
The local government approved a plan for urban cable cars by 2025, modeled on Medellín and La Paz and envisioned by urban strategist Vivian Arroyo, with wheelchair accessibility and priority seating.
A fleet of electric water taxis and ferries is due in 2024, with Marina Larsen, head of the Sustainable Mobility Project, emphasizing eased road traffic and electric propulsion.
